titleEn: Horse Kick to the Chest - Flail Segment

patient.name: Greg Hollis
patient.affectEn: anxious and grimacing; pale and sweaty; sitting on the aisle floor against a steel stall gate with his left hand pressed to his right chest; breathing fast and shallow and guarding the right side
patient.speechEn: short phrases, stopping to catch his breath; cooperative; answers only what he is asked, grimacing as he talks

scene.settingEn: Aisle of a horse boarding stable in Aldergrove, 1620 hrs call. The aisle is concrete with shavings, well lit and wide enough for the stretcher. The horse that kicked him is back in its stall behind a closed, latched door and is quiet; a second horse is tied at the far end of the aisle. One patient.
hazardsEn: the horse that kicked him - back in its stall behind a closed, latched door, quiet
a second horse tied at the far end of the aisle

bystanders.who: barn owner who met you at the aisle entrance
bystanders.knowsEn: saw it happen: the gelding struck out with a hind hoof while the man was brushing its flank, and the man was knocked backward about 3 m into the steel gate; he did not hit his head or lose consciousness; the owner put the horse back in its stall and called 911; willing to keep both horses and any onlookers clear and to open the gate and the doors if told exactly what to do

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: oxygen kit with non-rebreather mask and nasal cannula
hard cervical collars in several sizes
spinal device with foam blocks and straps
dressings and bandages for the forearm scrape
PCP: IV start kit and normal saline
PCP: PEEP valve for the BVM

dispatchEn: 1620 hrs. Code 3 to a horse boarding stable in Aldergrove. 44-year-old male kicked in the chest by a horse, having trouble breathing. The barn owner is with him. Langley Memorial Hospital is 14 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch update en route: the barn owner says the horse has been put back in its stall and the man is sitting on the aisle floor holding his right side; he is talking but keeps stopping to catch his breath.
arrivalEn: The barn owner meets you at the aisle entrance and leads you in. The horse is back in its stall behind a closed, latched door and is quiet; a second horse is tied at the far end of the aisle. The aisle is concrete with shavings, well lit and wide enough for the stretcher. The patient is sitting on the floor against a steel stall gate. The owner tells you he saw it happen: the gelding struck out with a hind hoof while the man was brushing its flank, and the man was knocked backward about 3 m into the gate. He did not hit his head or lose consciousness. One patient.
firstLookEn: A 44-year-old man sitting on the aisle floor against a steel stall gate, his left hand pressed to his right chest. He is pale and sweaty, anxious and grimacing, and breathing fast and shallow.

primary.locEn: Alert (AVPU = A), GCS 15. Oriented to person, place, time and event. He answers in short phrases.
primary.airwayEn: Clear and he is speaking. No blood or vomit.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 32, shallow, with accessory muscle use and guarding of the right chest. When the chest is exposed: a horseshoe-shaped bruise over the right lateral ribs and a segment of the right lateral chest wall that moves INWARD on inspiration and OUTWARD on expiration (paradoxical movement); crepitus on palpation over the right lateral chest; air entry decreased on the right; trachea midline, no JVD, no open wound. If the chest has not been exposed, give only the rate and quality and do not describe the segment. SpO2 89% on room air if checked before oxygen goes on.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 112, strong and regular; capillary refill 2 seconds. No external bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: When the chest is exposed: the findings in breathing above (horseshoe-shaped bruise over the right lateral ribs, paradoxical segment, crepitus, decreased air entry on the right, no open wound). Rest of the rapid body survey: head and neck no deformity and no midline tenderness; abdomen soft and non-tender; pelvis stable; limbs no deformity; back no deformity or tenderness when he is log-rolled. If asked, he has no new neurological deficit and is not intoxicated. Skin is given automatically during the RBS: pale and sweaty. Examiner notes - do not volunteer: the flail segment should be stabilized by hand at once (hand pressure by the partner, or the patient's own hand); nothing is taped or strapped across it and there is no wound, so no chest seal.

history.ccEn: My right side... I can't breathe in.

opqrst.oEn: Right when the horse kicked me, about fifteen minutes ago. I was brushing its flank and it struck out with a hind hoof, right into my chest. It threw me back into the steel gate.
opqrst.pEn: Every breath makes it worse. Moving makes it worse. Nothing makes it better.
opqrst.rEn: Right lower chest. It doesn't go anywhere else.
opqrst.tEn: About fifteen minutes ago, when the horse kicked me.

sample.sEn: Sharp pain in my right lower chest, I can't take a deep breath, and my heart is racing. No cough, no coughing blood. No neck pain, no back pain, no numbness or tingling, no belly pain.
sample.aEn: None that I know of. (If asked about NSAIDs, ibuprofen or acetaminophen specifically: "No, nothing like that either.")
sample.mEn: Atorvastatin, 20 milligrams once a day. No blood thinners. (Only if asked about pain pills, acetaminophen, Tylenol, ibuprofen or Advil today: "No, I haven't taken anything for pain today.")
sample.pEn: High cholesterol. No lung or heart problems, no bleeding problems, no liver problems, no stomach ulcers. I don't smoke. Two beers a week.
sample.lEn: A sandwich at 12:30 and a coffee at 3 o'clock.
sample.eEn: I was brushing the gelding's flank in the aisle when he struck out and kicked me with a hind hoof, right in the right side of the chest. It threw me back about three metres into the steel gate and I slid down onto the floor. I didn't hit my head and I didn't black out.

fe.generalEn: I'm fit and healthy. No recent illness.
fe.cnsEn: No headache, no dizziness, no numbness or tingling in my arms or legs.
fe.respiratoryEn: My right chest hurts and I'm short of breath. No cough, no coughing blood.
fe.cardiovascularEn: My heart is racing. No chest pressure. No palpitations before this happened.
fe.giGuEn: No nausea, no belly pain. My urine's normal.
fe.integumentaryEn: A bruise on my right chest and a scrape on my right forearm.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: Just the right chest wall. No neck, back or limb pain.
fe.eentEn: No change in my vision, no bleeding from my ears or nose, no pain in my face.

findings.headNeckEn: No wounds, no midline tenderness. Trachea midline, neck veins flat, no crepitus in the neck. If a collar has been applied it is in place.
findings.chestLungsEn: Horseshoe-shaped bruise over the right lateral ribs. A segment of the right lateral chest wall moves inward on inspiration and outward on expiration (paradoxical). Crepitus on palpation over the right lateral chest. Air entry decreased on the right and clear on the left in all 6 sites. No open wound. Trachea midline, no JVD.
findings.backEn: No deformity or tenderness at the log roll.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: No deformity. Circulation, sensation and movement intact in both legs.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: A scrape on the right forearm. No deformity. Circulation, sensation and movement intact in both arms.

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: en route, baseline before any analgesic

resp.character: accessory muscle use with guarding of the right chest

vitalsSets.spo2: 89% on room air before oxygen, 93% on 15 L NRB

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: about 6 minutes after set 1, en route - he is tiring and the oral analgesics have not yet taken effect; breathing now inadequate

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: He is changing. He is drowsy and confused now, his breathing is very rapid and very shallow, and his lips look dusky.
stateChanges.findingsIfAssessedEn: Trachea midline, no JVD. The vital signs are now those of vitals set 2 (the engine gives the readings).

vitalsPatch.spo2: 95% with assisted ventilations on 15 L oxygen

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan oxygen, BVM and suction, a collar and spinal device, and an early transport decision; anticipate a significant chest injury
triggers: bring a collar and the spinal device
this could be a load and go

expected.actionEn: Anticipate an animal hazard (a loose or kicking horse) in a barn aisle; gloves and eye protection ready; ask that the horse stays secured
triggers: make sure the horse is secured
ask the owner to secure the horse

expected.actionEn: Verbalize hazards (horse secured in its stall, a second horse tied at the far end, concrete floor), environment, mechanism (kicked in the chest and thrown about 3 m into a steel gate), number of patients (1)
triggers: the horse is secured in its stall
second horse is tied at the far end
mechanism is a kick from a horse

expected.actionEn: Don gloves and eye protection; ask the owner to keep both horses and any onlookers away from the patient
First look: sitting against the gate, hand pressed to the right chest, fast shallow breathing, pale and sweaty
Assess LOC / AVPU: Alert, GCS 15, fully oriented
triggers: do you know where you are

expected.actionEn: Decide the spine out loud with the BC SMR matrix and Modified NEXUS (p.26): no midline tenderness, alert and oriented, no deficit, not intoxicated - but the flail chest is a major distracting injury (and multiple rib fractures with lung injury are multi-trauma), so SMR is warranted; manually stabilize the head and neck, apply a hard collar, never tape the head (p.25-26)
triggers: manual stabilization of the head and neck
partner, hold his head in line

expected.actionEn: Assess airway: clear and he is speaking; keep it protected while the head and chest are stabilized
triggers: he's speaking so the airway is open

expected.actionEn: Expose and assess the chest: rate 32 and shallow with accessory muscle use, paradoxical segment, crepitus, decreased air entry on the right, SpO2 89% - recognize respiratory distress
Assess circulation: radial pulse 112, skin pale and sweaty, capillary refill 2 seconds, no external bleeding
triggers: rate and quality of the pulse

expected.actionEn: Complete the rapid body survey and MANUALLY stabilize the flail segment at once (p.34) - hand pressure over the segment by the partner or the patient's own hand; there is no open wound, so no chest seal; nothing taped or strapped across it
triggers: head to toe for other injuries

expected.actionEn: Note skin: pale and sweaty
High-flow oxygen 15 L by non-rebreather (trauma, respiratory distress, SpO2 89%) to keep SpO2 at or above 94%, with the BVM ready to assist ventilations

Position the patient ASAP (p.34) within SMR: supine on the spinal device or stretcher with the injured side supported by hand; the head of the stretcher is not raised because he has no head injury (p.26)
triggers: head of the stretcher stays flat
position him as soon as possible

expected.actionEn: Categorize as RTC and name the criteria: chest wall instability (flail chest) and respiratory distress with accessory muscle use (p.7)
Collared, packaged on the spinal device with the flail side supported, and ready to load within 15 minutes
Delegate effectively: the barn owner keeps the horses clear and opens the gate and doors, the partner prepares the device and cot, and a helper holds the flail and head steady during the roll
triggers: open the gate and the doors
partner, prepare the device and the cot
hold the flail while we roll

expected.actionEn: Establish chief complaint: right chest pain and difficulty breathing after a horse kick

HxC/C with OPQRST: mechanism (kick, then thrown into the gate), time (about 15 minutes), no head strike or LOC, pain character and what worsens it, cough or coughing blood, neck and back pain, neurological symptoms
triggers: does it hurt to breathe in

expected.actionEn: Pain score: 9/10, sharp, worse with breathing and movement
PMHx, including the screens needed for the analgesics: no liver disease, no ulcers, no bleeding problems
Medications: atorvastatin, no blood thinners, and specifically no acetaminophen or ibuprofen taken today
triggers: taken any Tylenol or ibuprofen today

expected.actionEn: Allergies: none known - including NSAIDs and acetaminophen
LOI: sandwich at 1230, coffee at 1500
GCS with components (15: E4 V5 M6)
BP by auscultation - baseline before any analgesic; systolic 138, so the Hypovolemia criteria are not met
Pulse rate/strength/rhythm
Respirations rate, depth and effort with the paradoxical segment and air entry on both sides
Skin hands-on: temperature, colour, moisture
Pupils
SpO2 on room air then on oxygen, recorded before any analgesic is considered
FE - General health
triggers: how have you been feeling lately

expected.actionEn: FE - CNS (numbness or tingling)
FE - Respiratory (pertinent)
FE - Cardiovascular
FE - GI/GU
FE - Integumentary
FE - Musculoskeletal
FE - Endocrine
FE - EENT
Head/neck exam: collar fit, midline tenderness, trachea, neck veins
Chest exam with 6-site auscultation and bilateral comparison, recheck the flail segment and watch for tension signs
Abdomen exam
Back exam during the log roll, with the flail side supported
triggers: run my hands down the back

expected.actionEn: Lower extremities with CSM
Upper extremities with CSM; dress the forearm scrape once the priorities are handled
Keep the flail segment manually stabilized through the log roll, the move to the cot and loading - nothing taped or strapped across it (p.34 'MANUALLY')
triggers: keep the flail stabilized through the roll
support the segment during the roll
hold the flail while we lift
nothing taped or strapped across the flail
flail stays supported through the move

expected.actionEn: Spinal management skill: manual head stabilization, correctly sized hard collar, head never taped, coordinated log roll with the flail side supported, then the spinal device with foam blocks and the body secured only where appropriate (Full SMR) or the stretcher mattress rather than a clamshell (Simple SMR) (p.25-26)
triggers: log roll with the flail side supported
secure the body then the head

expected.actionEn: Withhold Entonox and say why: a pneumothorax cannot be ruled out (crepitus, decreased right air entry) and is a listed contraindication - nitrous oxide expands a closed air space; the altered LOC at set 2 is a second reason (p.65)
triggers: nitrous expands a closed air space

expected.actionEn: Give BOTH acetaminophen 1000 mg PO and ibuprofen 400 mg PO, after ruling out each contraindication aloud (p.58, p.68), while he is still alert, with the six rights
triggers: no liver disease and no overdose concern
no ulcers or bleeding and no anticoagulants

expected.actionEn: PCP: do NOT apply CPAP - a traumatic cause of respiratory distress and a possible pneumothorax are listed contraindications (p.52); use the BVM when breathing is inadequate
PCP: obtain vascular access en route (p.34, p.38); say that the fluid bolus (needs systolic under 90, p.54) and TXA (needs signs of shock, p.78) are not indicated
Reassess ABCs, the flail stabilization and SpO2 after every move and every 5 minutes

Recognize that breathing is now inadequate (38, very shallow, SpO2 86% on 15 L, falling LOC) and begin assisted ventilations with a BVM and 15 L oxygen at once, timed with his own breaths (p.11, p.34)
Assist ventilations with the BVM connected to oxygen: good mask seal, visible chest rise, flail segment kept stabilized
Second full set of vitals within 5-6 minutes; interpret the trend out loud as a tiring patient with failing breathing, and upgrade the hospital notification
Monitor for tension pneumothorax (p.34): tracheal shift, JVD, absent right air entry, falling BP - none yet - and say what you would report
triggers: absent air entry on the right
I would report a tension pneumothorax

expected.actionEn: Reassess the pain (9/10), note that the oral analgesics have not yet taken effect, and document that Entonox stays withheld and why
triggers: pain is still nine out of ten
the analgesics haven't taken effect yet

expected.actionEn: En-route notification for a critical patient: flail chest, failing breathing needing assisted ventilations, SMR in place
Complete hand-off with mechanism, flail segment findings, vitals trend, SMR reason, oral analgesics with times, Entonox withheld and why, and when assisted ventilations began
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes with drug times, the Entonox contraindication and the change in breathing

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate starts spinal motion restriction: manual stabilization of the head and neck, a hard collar, or the spinal device / stretcher SMR (good act; also detected from the candidate's words)

candidate (or the partner on the candidate's instruction) lets go of manual head and neck stabilization before the patient is secured on the spinal device with the collar on and the head blocks in place; applying the collar alone does not permit release
candidate tapes the patient's head to the spinal device

candidate (or the partner or the patient's own hand on the candidate's instruction) manually stabilizes the flail segment with hand pressure over it (good act; also detected from the candidate's words)

candidate or the partner lets go of the manual support over the flail segment and it is not re-established, or the candidate directs the log roll, the lift to the cot or the load while saying nobody is supporting the segment; do not report a move only because support was not mentioned in that sentence

candidate stabilizes the flail segment with circumferential tape, a tight strap or bandage around the chest, or a dressing or chest seal taped over the segment (the ordinary body straps of a spinal device are NOT this event unless the candidate presents them as the stabilization)

candidate (or the partner on the candidate's instruction) begins assisted ventilations with the bag-valve mask (good act; also detected from the candidate's words); a plan or 'BVM ready' is not this event

AFTER the examiner has described the change in the patient (drowsy and confused, breathing very rapid and very shallow, dusky lips), the candidate carries on with other tasks over the next several turns (history, Functional Enquiry, exam, analgesics, notification, paperwork) without beginning BVM-assisted ventilations. Reassessing the airway, breathing, LOC, GCS or SpO2 and asking for vitals is NOT carrying on - it is how the candidate recognizes the change. Report only after at least three further candidate lines with no assisted ventilations and no stated intention to start them, never in the same turn the change is first described, and never once assisted-ventilations-started has been recorded.
candidate gives or states an acetaminophen dose outside 500-1000 mg PO or an ibuprofen dose outside 300-400 mg PO (for example 2 g of acetaminophen or 800 mg of ibuprofen)

AFTER the examiner has described him as drowsy and confused (the change in breathing and LOC), the candidate gives or hands him an oral medication (acetaminophen or ibuprofen) or tells him to swallow one
PCP gives a fluid bolus (runs normal saline wide open or orders a set volume such as 20 mL/kg or 500 mL); starting an IV with a saline lock or TKVO is NOT this event
candidate lets or asks the patient to stand up or walk (for example to the cot or the ambulance)

drugs.doseEn: 1000 mg PO (guideline range 500 - 1000 mg PO; may repeat once after 4 hours - not if given within the past 4 hours; contraindicated in severe liver disease or suspected overdose). Indicated here for his pain and given while he is alert, after baseline vitals with SpO2.

400 mg PO (guideline range 300 - 400 mg PO; may repeat every 4-6 hours; contraindicated with NSAID hypersensitivity, active GI hemorrhage or ulcers, or anticoagulants). Indicated here for his pain and given while he is alert, after baseline vitals with SpO2; may be given together with acetaminophen.

self-administered by inhalation - WITHHELD in this scenario: a pneumothorax cannot be ruled out (crepitus, decreased air entry on the right) and pneumothorax is a listed contraindication; altered level of consciousness at set 2 is a second contraindication. A statement of withholding it is NOT drug:entonox.

3 mL self-administered via inhaler - not part of Appendix A pain management; its CHECK caution (cardiac instability or respiratory depression, altered consciousness) argues against it here. A statement of withholding it is NOT a dose.

NOT indicated and contraindicated here: traumatic cause of respiratory distress and a suspected pneumothorax; later also falling LOC and failing respirations (these patients need a BVM). A statement of withholding it is NOT drug:cpap.
drugs.indicationsEn: 13 years or older in significant respiratory distress, awake and following commands, RR > 24, SpO2 < 94% on oxygen and accessory muscle use - but the contraindications below apply
drugs.contraindicationsEn: traumatic cause of respiratory distress; suspected or known pneumothorax; decreased level of consciousness; imminent or actual respiratory failure (slow or shallow respirations with falling LOC) - ventilate with a BVM instead

drugs.doseEn: 2 g (2000 mg) IV push over 1 minute - NOT indicated: systolic 138 and no signs of shock; give only for major trauma after initiation of the Hypovolemia protocol or signs of shock with a mechanism or findings suggesting ongoing bleeding. A statement that it is not indicated is NOT drug:txa.
drugs.indicationsEn: major trauma after initiation of the Hypovolemia protocol; signs of shock in association with the mechanism or findings suggesting occult or ongoing bleeding - currently not met
drugs.contraindicationsEn: known hypersensitivity or allergy to TXA; more than 3 hours after injury; patient under 12 years; isolated TBI
drugs.cautionsEn: further hypotension if administered too quickly

drugs.doseEn: vascular access en route if required (Chest Trauma); a fluid bolus (20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing every 500 mL) is NOT indicated - the Hypovolemia protocol needs systolic under 90 and he is at 138

His eyes are open on their own, his answers are confused, and he obeys commands." (the actor cannot show the fall in LOC; the GCS itself is spoken by the engine). Before that change he is alert and fully oriented.
examinerPrompts.breathingNotDepictedEn: The actor cannot show the paradoxical movement: when the candidate exposes the chest, state that there is a horseshoe-shaped bruise over the right lateral ribs and a segment of the right lateral chest wall that moves inward on inspiration and outward on expiration, with crepitus on palpation and decreased air entry on the right. If the chest has not been exposed, give only the rate and quality. trackNotes.emrEn: EMR gives manual flail stabilization, spinal motion restriction (hard collar, spinal device), high-flow oxygen, assisted ventilations with a BVM when breathing fails, oral acetaminophen and ibuprofen, and rapid transport within 15 minutes; Entonox is withheld with the reason said aloud. EMR does NOT start an IV or give a fluid bolus or TXA, and there is no Functional Enquiry.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds vascular access en route (Chest Trauma, 'if required') and the 9-system Functional Enquiry, and must say what is NOT indicated: no CPAP (traumatic cause and possible pneumothorax, p.52), no fluid bolus (systolic 138; the Hypovolemia protocol needs under 90, p.54) and no TXA (no signs of shock, p.78). A PEEP valve on the BVM is a PCP option (p.50-52) but, with a possible pneumothorax, the candidate should name the risk aloud. Methoxyflurane is not part of Appendix A and carries a respiratory-depression caution (p.71). Textbook practice - not a BC rubric item: a folded pad held by hand on the flail segment gives the same support as bare hands.

sourcePages: Scenario tr-11 (data/practical/scenarios-2.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport, history, vitals sets 1-2 (set 2 about 6 minutes after set 1: GCS 14, 38 very shallow, SpO2 86% on 15 L; 95% once ventilations are assisted, 82% if not), FE, exam, interventions, ongoing, handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 RTC criteria (chest wall instability or deformity i.e. flail chest; respiratory distress), p.11 Primary Survey Interventions (assisting inadequate or failing respirations; oxygen for trauma and respiratory distress), p.25-26 Spinal Management (NEXUS / Canadian C-Spine; manually stabilize the head and neck, hard collar, spinal immobilization device, foam blocks, do not tape the head), p.34 Chest Trauma (MANUALLY stabilize flail chest, assist oxygenation and ventilation, position the patient ASAP; PCP vascular access en route if required), p.38 IV procedures, p.50-52 Oxygen Administration, CPAP and PEEP (CPAP contraindicated for a traumatic cause of respiratory distress, suspected or known pneumothorax and failing respirations; BVM instead), p.54 Hypovolemia (systolic under 90 with shock; fluid bolus 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L reassessing every 500 mL), p.58 Acetaminophen (500 - 1,000 mg PO, not within 4 hours of a prior dose, severe liver disease, may be used with ibuprofen), p.65 Entonox (contraindications pneumothorax and altered level of consciousness; baseline vital signs including SpO2 first), p.68 Ibuprofen (300-400 mg PO; hypersensitivity to NSAIDs, active GI hemorrhage or ulcers, anticoagulants), p.71 Methoxyflurane (CHECK cautions), p.78 Tranexamic Acid (indications, 2 g IV push over 1 minute).
